chunks: ʿAlī ibn Ibrāhīm narrated from his father, from Ibn Maḥbūb, from al-ʿAlāʾ ibn Razīn, from Muḥammad ibn Muslim, who said:
I asked Abā Jaʿfar عليه السلام about a man who accuses his son of zina. He said: “If he were to kill him, he would not be killed for him; and if he accuses him, the hadd is not administered for him.”

I said: What if his father accuses his mother? He said: “If he accuses her and disowns her child, the two engage in liʿān, that child whom he disowned is not ascribed to him, they are separated from one another, and she does not become lawful for him.”
He said: “And if he says to his son, while his mother is alive, ‘O son of an adulteress,’ and he does not disown her child, the hadd is administered for her, and they are not separated.”

He said: “And if he says to his son, ‘O son of an adulteress,’ while his mother is deceased, and she has no one to claim her right against him except her child from him, then the hadd is not carried out against him, because the right to the hadd has passed to his child from her. But if she has a child from someone other than him, then that one is her representative, and the hadd is administered for him. And if she has no child from someone other than him, but she has relatives who uphold the right of the hadd, then the hadd is administered for them.”

key_terms.الزِّنَى: illicit sexual intercourse; the offense alleged in the accusation
key_terms.انْتَفَى: he disowned or denied attribution of the child
key_terms.تَلَاعَنَا: the spouses engage in mutual imprecation (liʿān)
key_terms.وَلِيُّهَا: her legal representative who claims her right

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling if a father accuses his son or the child’s mother of zina in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith sets out legal rulings concerning qadhf within the family, especially when a father accuses his son or the mother of zina. It distinguishes between cases involving direct accusation, denial of paternity, liʿān, and who has standing to demand the hadd after the woman's death.
